additional_requirements: depressive_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness (Criterion C)
delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode (Criterion B)

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.

subtypes.Derailment or Loose Associations: A speech pattern of switching rapidly from one topic to another with no logical connection between thoughts.
subtypes.Tangentiality: Speech that deviates entirely from the question and fails to answer directly.
subtypes.Incoherence or Word Salad: Severe fragmentation of speech and sentence structure, making it nearly impossible to understand.
subtypes.Neologisms: Using made-up words that have meaning only to the individual.
subtypes.Clang Associations: Speech governed by sounds, such as rhyming, rather than the meaning of words.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

patient_info.stressor: After a rent increase and mounting repairs on the small house he had shared with his late wife, Charles moved into a subsidized senior apartment farther from his church, marina, garden plot, and the neighbors who had anchored his weekly routine. Over the next 1 year and 5 months, the disruption of familiar places and roles coincided with a gradual loss of interest in choir rehearsals, bridge club, cooking, and handyman jobs, while his thinking became harder for others to follow and fixed suspicious beliefs began interfering with ordinary interactions. His appetite and pace of activity changed noticeably, and periods of hopelessness and thoughts of death made it difficult for him to manage bills, attend volunteer commitments, or keep appointments reliably. He came to psychiatric care after a church outreach coordinator, already concerned by his absence from gospel rehearsal and disorganized behavior at a senior-center workshop, helped him arrange an urgent evaluation through a community mental health clinic.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I came in because I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings and slipping notes about me to the office, even though everybody keeps telling me it's just notices on the doors.

S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.
S021.manifestation: When I try to explain things, I start with the rent, then the marina, then the choir robes and the wires in the walls, and people look at me like I skipped half the story.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.
S022.manifestation: At the senior-center workshop I kept lining up the screws by size and tapping the table instead of fixing the shelf, and when the lady asked me to sit down I just stood there holding the screwdriver like I couldn't switch gears.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day already went bad before I even get my feet on the floor.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to look forward to choir practice, bridge, cooking beans on Sunday, and doing little repair jobs for folks, but now I mostly let the phone ring and tell myself there is no point going.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: I forget to eat until late in the day, and my pants have been hanging loose because coffee and a piece of toast feel like all I can manage.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.
S028.manifestation: Some days I move so slow getting dressed or walking to the mailbox that old neighbors would not know me, and other days I pace my little apartment checking the window over and over.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: Bills and appointment cards pile up because I read the same line again and again and still can't decide what needs doing first.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: I don't have a plan to hurt myself, but I do catch myself thinking it would be all right if I just didn't wake up and had nothing more to mess up.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: When I am down in that hollow place and barely eating or answering the phone, I am also most sure the apartment people are tracking me and talking to the office about me.

additional_requirement_2.name: Additional Requirement 2
additional_requirement_2.description: depressive_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness (Criterion C)
additional_requirement_2.manifestation: For most of the time since I moved, even on days when I could sound a little clearer, I still felt low, useless, and uninterested in the things I used to do.

additional_requirement_3.name: Additional Requirement 3
additional_requirement_3.description: delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode (Criterion B)
additional_requirement_3.manifestation: There was a spell of several weeks when I was eating a bit better and not waking up so hopeless, but I still believed the neighbors were watching my door and reporting on me.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I have fallen behind on bills, missed appointments, and stopped showing up for church and volunteer commitments because I cannot keep my days organized or trust ordinary interactions.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about a year and five months, since I left the house I shared with my wife and moved into the senior apartment.

psychotic_symptoms_duration.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
psychotic_symptoms_duration.manifestation: The suspicious thoughts about the apartment neighbors and office have been with me for about a year and a month.

depressive_episode_duration.name: Depressive Episode Duration
depressive_episode_duration.manifestation: The heavy, no-point feeling and pulling away from things have been going on for about a year and two months.
